candidates.tagline: Bristol renamed its SS Great Britain museum. The ship still says Great Britain.
candidates.story: Bristol's 'Brunel's SS Great Britain' museum site has been rebranded as 'Bristol Dockyards' — stripping 'Great Britain' from the organisational name of a museum whose entire centrepiece is a ship still officially called SS Great Britain.
candidates.why_funny: The museum removed the most recognisable words from its own brand name, but the enormous iron ship in the middle of it still shouts 'GREAT BRITAIN!' at every visitor.
candidates.alt: The bow of the SS Great Britain in its Bristol dry dock, with tall masts and signal flags above and a banner reading 'GREAT BRITAIN!' visible at the waterline

candidates.tagline: 7 years of FIFA pitch research. France wore flat shoes anyway.
candidates.story: After seven years of engineering research, FIFA installed Tahoma 31 Bermudagrass at MetLife Stadium — the World Cup Final venue — but France coach Deschamps said it 'might be cement below the grass,' midfielder Rabiot called it 'more like an artificial surface,' and Brazil's Vinicius said it dries out so fast the ball slows mid-game.
candidates.why_funny: Seven years and millions of dollars of sports-science turf research produced a field the world's best players refuse to wear studs on.
candidates.alt: France's Kylian Mbappé stretching to reach the ball on the bright green Bermuda grass pitch at MetLife Stadium during the France vs Senegal World Cup Group I match on 16 June 2026
